settings.title: Deck Height
settings.text:
Standard Height:
Each kit comes ready to assemble at 15–17 inches off the ground.

Increase Height:
Use longer posts to raise the deck. We also offer longer post kits with bracing. Chat with our design specialists for details.

Decrease Height:
Dig a few inches where the footings sit to lower the deck.

We offer different height post kits:
Each kit includes the posts and bracing. Contact our design team for more details.

settings.title: Uneven Ground
settings.text:
Even if your yard isn’t perfectly flat, your deck can be. Just cut the posts to level things out, or use our longer post when you need more height.

Pro Tip:
On slightly uneven ground, use gravel or cement tiles under the posts to even out the height.

We offer different height post kits:
Each kit includes the posts and bracing. Contact our design team for more details.

settings.headline: Backyard went from blah to WOW!!!
settings.review_text:
My wife and I wanted to make better use of a portion of our backyard and transform it into something both practical and enjoyable. To create more usable space facing our swimming pool, we decided to remove a built-in grill island that I had constructed in the early 2000s. This opened up the area and gave us the opportunity to create a true outdoor living and entertainment space rather than simply maintaining a patch of grass.

After many discussions about our vision for the space, we decided on a wood deck topped with a pergola. Our goal was to create a dedicated entertainment and relaxation area overlooking the shallow end of the pool, where family and friends could gather and enjoy the outdoors.

As with any project I take on, I devoted a significant amount of time to research. I reviewed hundreds of photos, studied landscaping concepts, compared deck designs, and explored numerous options before making a decision. After extensive evaluation, I chose A-DIY as the deck provider for several key reasons: competitive pricing, the kit-based assembly system, the warranty, and the fact that the product was engineered by professionals. I was particularly impressed by the thoughtful design. Everything arrived pre-measured, pre-cut, pre-drilled, and complete with all the necessary hardware, making the process incredibly efficient.

The ordering process was straightforward and user-friendly. I reviewed the available layouts and dimensions, selected the design that best suited our space, and was pleasantly surprised to receive a discount as well.

A few weeks after placing the order, three pallets of materials arrived. I reviewed the plans and overall design concept with my handyman so he could fully understand the intended look and layout. He was immediately impressed by the quality of the materials and confidently stated that the deck could be assembled in days rather than weeks.

He was absolutely right. The entire project took approximately eight days to complete. Along the way, we incorporated a few custom touches, including a built-in step and wrap-around skirting to prevent animals from nesting beneath the deck.

Since completing the deck and pergola, we've hosted several gatherings with family and friends. The feedback has been overwhelmingly positive:

“Oh my God, that's beautiful!”
“That came from a kit?”
“It took less than 10 days to build?”
“This looks like something you'd see at a resort!”

My wife and I couldn't agree more. We are absolutely thrilled with our decision to choose an A-DIY deck. From the initial consultation and material selection process to delivery and assembly, every aspect of the experience exceeded our expectations.

As an engineer myself, I have a deep appreciation for good design and thoughtful execution. The engineering, material quality, packaging, instructions, logistics, and overall assembly process reflect a tremendous amount of planning and attention to detail. Kudos to the entire A-DIY team, from the designers and manufacturing staff to the shipping and customer service teams, for creating such an exceptional product.

The finished deck has completely transformed our backyard. Not only does it look incredible, but with the durability of the Trex materials, we're confident it will provide years of enjoyment and stand the test of time.

Thank you, A-DIY, for delivering an outstanding product, a seamless ordering experience, and excellent customer service. We couldn't be happier with the result.

settings.question: How big is a 16x20 deck, really?
settings.answer: It is a nominal 16 ft × 20 ft, about 320 sq ft of finished deck. Final assembled dimensions can vary slightly because of framing, board spacing and the picture-frame border, so leave a little clearance at your site.

settings.question: How much does a 16x20 deck cost?
settings.answer: The A-DIY 16x20 pressure-treated wood deck kit is [price], with taxes and shipping calculated at checkout. During the Fall Sale the code [code] brings it to [sale_price]. The price includes all engineered parts, Tuff Block footings, galvanized hardware and drill bit, so there is no separate materials list, and A-DIY kits run 30–50% less than hiring a contractor (see how much a deck costs in your state).

settings.question: How long does it take to build a 16x20 wood deck kit?
settings.answer: Plan on a weekend. One 16x20 customer built the full deck in one weekend with two people and a drill. Because the kit is modular, a larger footprint mostly means more of the same repeating steps, not harder ones.

settings.question: Do I need experience or special tools?
settings.answer: No. A standard power drill is the only tool, the drill bit, step-by-step instructions and the 3D instructional app are included. There is no cutting and no measuring.

settings.question: How high does the deck sit, and can I change it?
settings.answer: Each kit is ready to assemble at 15–17 inches off the ground. Longer post kits with bracing raise it; digging a few inches where the footings sit lowers it.

settings.question: What if my yard isn’t flat?
settings.answer:
Even if your yard isn’t perfectly flat, your deck can be. Just cut the posts to level things out, or use our longer post when you need more height. On a 16x20 footprint it is worth checking the level across the whole area before you start, since a slope shows more over 20 feet than over 12.

Pro Tip:
On slightly uneven ground, use gravel or cement tiles under the posts to even out the height.

We offer different height post kits:
Each kit includes the posts and bracing. Contact our design team for more details.

settings.question: Do I need a permit for a 16x20 deck?
settings.answer: Permit rules are set by your local municipality and depend on height, size and placement. Many areas only exempt small, low platforms, so a 320 sq ft deck is more likely to need a permit than a small one — check with your building department before you build. Engineering diagrams are available to support an application.

settings.question: How does the kit arrive?
settings.answer: Crated, by LTL ground freight, typically within 10–14 business days. The carrier contacts you to schedule curbside delivery. Parts are packed in order of use, so you can build over several evenings without lumber scattered across the yard.

settings.question: Wood or composite: which 16x20 deck kit should I choose?
settings.answer: Both use the same engineered system. The pressure-treated wood 16x20 is [price], carries a 5-year structural warranty and can be stained to match your home. The composite 16x20 is [twin_price] in Amazon Gray or Forest Wood, with a 25-year warranty on the composite deck boards and minimal maintenance — on a deck this size, skipping the re-staining is worth weighing. See the 16x20 composite deck page for the full details.

settings.question: What warranty comes with the wood kit?
settings.answer: Every pressure-treated wood kit carries a 5-year structural warranty.

settings.question: Can I pay for my 16x20 over time?
settings.answer: Yes. Choose A-DIY’s 0% interest payment plan in 4, 6 or 8 monthly payments (ships after the final payment), or finance through Affirm, Klarna or Shop Pay with 0% APR options up to 24 months, subject to credit approval.
